Universities ranked by finance publication counts

Universities ranked by finance publication counts by university. Expand a row to inspect the sampled faculty and top authors.
Rank University Faculty

Scroll for more columns →

Finance faculty rosters and publications use independently gathered data from official faculty directories, publication records, and citation indexes. Expand a school to inspect its roster and any linked directory. Scores reflect matched records. Rankings use current faculty in universities with at least five faculty. Each faculty author receives journal credit for an article. The expanded selection assigns half credit to additional journals. Raw per capita divides by the sampled faculty count. Bayes adds 5 to that denominator. Top four sums the four highest-scoring faculty members.

Considers citations for journal publications
Universities ranked by finance citations by university. Expand a row to inspect the sampled faculty and top authors.
Rank University Articles scored

Scroll for more columns →

Finance faculty rosters and publications use independently gathered data from official faculty directories, publication records, and citation indexes. Expand a school to inspect its roster and any linked directory. Scores reflect matched records. Rankings use current faculty in universities with at least five faculty. Each faculty author receives one credit for an article in the Top-3 finance or Top-5 economics journals. Citation-weighted credits multiply article credit by the matched OpenAlex count. Recent windows count citations received in the last complete calendar years, independently of the publication cutoff. Raw per capita divides by the sampled faculty count. Bayes adds 5 to that denominator. Top four sums the four highest-scoring faculty members.

These data are meant to help faculty, students, and prospective students start their research. Important decisions should be based on the actual data points after you have checked them, not the scores and certainly not the ranks. I am Will Gornall, a finance professor - I focused on the finance data and rankings and added other rankings on a best-effort basis using the econ-atlas data. I am also a Stanford GSB graduate, a UBC professor, and the director of UBC’s finance PhD program which creates biases, however, I have made what I see as neutral methodological choices and allowed you to customize them. This is an independent project, developed without institutional input from UBC.

- Will Gornall
